summary: Redwood AE + SE walked Pegasus Retail team through the Redwood Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for a checkout assistant and catalog search reranker. Key concerns: latency at peak traffic, cost per 1000 queries, compliance (SOC2 & KMS), and VPC connectivity for pilot. Next steps: pricing + pilot, benchmark run, share security docs, staging VPC details.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-31 14:00 PST | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Maya, Liam, Aria (Redwood) / Jared, Sofia, Priya, Ethan (Pegasus)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, happy almost new year, thanks for joining, i'm maya from redwood, i'll kick us off and liam will jump into the console walkthrough.
[00:12] Jared: thanks maya, appreciate it, we'll try to keep questions inline — sofia and priya will chime in for infra and ml.
[00:18] Maya: perfect, quick agenda: high-level console usage analytics, per-route dashboards, cost breakdowns and recommendations from optimize, then q&a and next steps.
[00:28] Liam: ok jumping in, so here is the main usage dashboard, you'll see token distribution over time, per-route breakdown, and cost by model variant. note — timestamps on these are approximate, the dashboard refreshes every minute.
[00:45] [00:45] Liam: (screen) the top left shows total tokens and revenue-equivalent cost, we map billing to model families, and you can filter by route or by api key.
[01:12] Sofia: quick question — can we group by customer id within a route? we have multi-tenant frontends.
[01:20] Liam: yes, you can add a dimension by client_id, that will show you cost per tenant. it's in the per-route viz. a little caveat: we anonymize PII by default unless you opt-in on dedicated/private.
[01:35] Priya: what's retention on these logs? we need 13 months for audit purposes.
[01:42] Maya: good call — retention is configurable depending on plan, hosted defaults to 90 days, enterprise tiers (dedicated/private) can push to long-term storage and we have add-ons for extended retention. we'll share the doc.
[01:56] [02:00] Liam: moving to per-route dashboard for "checkout-assistant" route — you'll see avg latency p50/p90, tokens/request, and cost per 1k requests broken down by model variant.
[02:18] Liam: notice here the p90 increases with long context windows, we recommend prefix caching for common product prompts to save on tokens.
[02:30] Jared: when you say "prefix caching" do you mean kv cache or something else?
[02:34] Liam: yes KV cache — our runtime keeps a KV cache of prefix tokens when requests share the same context. sometimes the transcription says K-V cash — that's a comical one we've seen — but it's KV cache.
[02:46] Sofia: sweet. also, how accurate is the cost model? our CFO will want predictable estimates.
[02:54] Maya: the console shows both estimated and realized cost. realized is actual billing; estimated uses per-token model profiles. there's also a cost simulator where you can inject traffic shapes to forecast monthly spend.
[03:10] [03:10] Liam: here's the cost breakdown panel — you can see cost by token, by model, by route. the optimize tab suggests batching and quantization for heavy routes like "catalog-search-rerank".
[03:27] Priya: any latency tradeoffs when quantizing?
[03:31] Liam: minimal for our quant profiles on T4/H100— usually small delta, depends on model; optimize will show expected latency and quality delta. we can run a quality regression job against your eval set.
[03:48] Ethan: we run peak flashes at midnight during promos, latency there is critical. Could you run sustained 200 RPS benchmarks?
[03:56] Liam: yes, that's exactly what we do in a pilot. we'll bring dedicated pools if you need guaranteed throughput. hosted can burst but dedicated gives you pinned capacity.
[04:10] [04:10] Maya: to clarify, dedicated = reserved GPU pools w/ SLA; private = your VPC or on-prem with control plane options. most customers start hosted, do a pilot for dedicated if they need predictability or isolation.
[04:26] Jared: what about encryption and KMS — we can't send any PII to a managed endpoint.
[04:33] Maya: for private you can integrate with your KMS/HSM and we support customer-managed keys. hosted has in-transit and at-rest encryption but if customer-managed keys are required we recommend private.
[04:47] Sofia: do you have SOC 2 and ISO certs?
[04:50] Maya: yes — SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001, we'll share the pack. we also provide audit logs per request on enterprise plans.
[05:02] [05:02] Liam: back to the console — here's a per-route anomaly detector; it flags sudden token spikes or quality regressions, and ties them to a prompt set so you can see which prompts trigger regressions.
[05:20] Priya: that would help with debugging. can we hook that into our pager?
[05:23] Liam: yep webhook and slack integrations; also datadog export.
[05:28] [05:30] Liam: demoing the cost simulator — you can upload sample traffic CSV and it will output expected monthly spend across model variants and recommendations to hit a target unit-cost.
[05:44] Jared: curious about model fallbacks — if a region is saturated can requests be routed to a cheaper model?
[05:50] Liam: yes smart routing policies: you can set cost-first fallback or latency-first; we also support regional fallbacks and automatic rollbacks.
[06:02] Sofia: in practice how often do you see quality regressions when fallback happens?
[06:06] Liam: we surface expected quality delta. for critical routes you can set a quality budget — fallback won't be used if it exceeds the budget.
[06:15] [06:20] Maya: ok quick pause — so far key asks: pegasus needs predictable cost at 200 RPS peaks, SOC2 + KMS details, and a pilot to benchmark hosted vs dedicated vs private. is that accurate?
[06:30] Jared: yes and we want a per-tenant cost view.
[06:34] Maya: noted.
[06:38] [06:40] Liam: showing Optimize recommendations for "catalog-search-rerank" — quantize to int8 (recommended on this model) and enable request-level batching of up to 16 requests; expected cost drop ~45% with <5% quality delta on our eval.
[06:58] Priya: sounds good, will you run the eval against our prod-ish dataset?
[07:03] Liam: yes that is standard in a pilot; we'll run the regression and share the test harness.
[07:10] [07:10] Ethan: what about per-token throttling? our frontend wants graceful degradation not hard failures.
[07:16] Liam: we have per-route throttles and auto-fallback to a cheaper model, plus cached responses for common prompts for graceful degradation.
[07:26] Sofia: any limitations on long context with KV cache? we have 20k token product catalogs in some calls.
[07:33] Liam: the runtime supports large context but performance depends on hardware and model. for very long contexts we recommend prefix caching + chunking and a retriever layer where appropriate.
[07:45] [07:45] Maya: i want to call out the per-route dashboard export — you can export flattened CSVs with cost attribution per request for finance.
[07:55] Jared: that's huge for our forecasting.
[08:00] [08:00] Liam: moving to security: here's the security pack link (shared in chat) — includes SOC2 report, encryption options, RBAC, SSO/SAML, and audit log samples.
[08:15] Priya: we use okta and terraform for infra — SSO and terraform-friendly infra is a must.
[08:19] Maya: SSO via SAML/okta supported; we also have terraform modules for dedicated/private deployments and a terraform provider.
[08:30] Sofia: how do you handle data residency in EU? we have EU customers.
[08:34] Maya: region-based routing and data residency controls available on enterprise/private, hosted also has EU regions. we'll map that in the pilot.
[08:45] [08:50] Liam: quick note on logs — we can stream request logs to your s3 with server-side encryption using your KMS.
[08:58] Priya: great.
[09:02] [09:05] Maya: ok any blockers on going to pilot? pricing concerns?
[09:10] Jared: cost — CFO wants guaranteed unit cost at scale; they're nervous about per-token surprises.
[09:15] Maya: understood — for dedicated we provide committed capacity and predictable unit economics; we'll include a model for commit vs usage-based in the proposal.
[09:28] Sofia: one more technical: for private on-prem, what's the control plane architecture?
[09:33] Liam: private control plane can be customer-managed or hosted; the data plane runs in your VPC and we provide a controller and a small operator; sometimes transcription will say "control plane is private" as "control plane is priva" — minor transcription oddities.
[09:48] [10:00] Liam: i'll show a quick runbook for the benchmark: we do warmup, 10-minute sustained run at target RPS, measure p50/p90 and cost, then run a quality regression on your eval set. we gather KV hit rates and effective tokens saved.
[10:18] Priya: timeline for pilot?
[10:21] Maya: we can start infra prep week of Jan 4, benchmarks week of Jan 11, results by Jan 18.
[10:28] Jared: good.
[10:32] [10:35] Maya: action recap: maya send pricing and pilot proposal (by jan 5), liam prepare benchmark scripts (by jan 7), priya share staging VPC details (by jan 4). we'll share security docs now.
[10:50] [10:50] Ethan: any concerns about rate limits on hosted trial?
[10:53] Liam: hosted trial has soft limits; for the pilot we'll request elevated limits or use dedicated pools to match your traffic.
[11:05] Sofia: if we do dedicated how long to provision?
[11:08] Maya: depends on capacity but typically a few days for reserved pools, if it's immediate we can burst on hosted while dedicated provisions.
[11:18] [11:20] Priya: are there any prerequisites from our side for the eval harness?
[11:24] Liam: we need a sample eval set, access to staging endpoints, and for private we'll need network peering / VPN info.
[11:34] Jared: we'll pull a 5k prompt eval set and share.
[11:37] Maya: perfect. thanks everyone, we'll send notes and links in the next 24 hours. happy new year!
[11:45] (call ends)

Notes on transcription quality: medium — occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "K-V cash", "priva"). Some speaker labels simplified.
